methodological_rigor.justification: Solid retrospective cohort with PSM balancing baseline characteristics (SMD<0.2). Thoughtful resectability subgroup analysis addresses selection bias inherent to treatment allocation. Multivariate Cox regression with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Single-center limitation acknowledged.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Directly informs clinical decision-making for T4 ESCC treatment selection. PSM strengthens causal inference. Comparison of nCT+S vs nCT+dCRT addresses active clinical controversy. Findings support surgery-first approach for responsive tumors, high clinical impact.

reporting_quality.justification: Complete Methods describing patient selection, treatment protocols, endpoints. Comprehensive Results with Kaplan-Meier curves, multivariate analyses, subgroup findings reported with Bonferroni adjustment. Data availability statement absent.

novelty_literature.justification: Compares nCT+S vs nCT+dCRT in T4 ESCC; novel in this specific subgroup. Extends known modalities to high-risk population. Addresses documented gap in long-term T4 outcome data. Confirms biological plausibility of surgery post-downstaging.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with detailed Methods enabling reproducibility. Results section clearly presents survival curves, multivariable analyses, subgroup findings. Discussion thoroughly contextualizes within CROSS/EMBRACE trials. Figures 4-5 effectively communicate subgroup results.

key_strengths: PSM with standardized mean difference <0.2 effectively balances baseline confounders including cT stage distribution
Resectability subgroup analysis (MDT-confirmed cases) minimizes selection bias from preferential allocation of complex tumors to surgery
Bonferroni correction applied to subgroup analyses reducing false positive inflation from multiple testing
Substantial follow-up (median 77 months) adequate for 3-year, 5-year survival assessment; clinically meaningful 11.7% LC advantage
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design limits generalizability; treatment allocation may reflect institutional preference beyond clinical criteria
Imaging heterogeneity: MRI-based planning for 3D-PTIB vs CT for F-3DIB may systematically favor surgical group in target delineation
No external validation; findings require prospective RCT confirmation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Strong comparative effectiveness study addressing clinical controversy in T4 ESCC. PSM and resectability subgroup analysis mitigate confounding. Significant OS/LC benefits demonstrated. Tier 2 appropriate given clinical relevance and PSM-balanced design, though single-center design and lack of external validation preclude Tier 1.
